title: Lost records and music; decline of club activity
summary: She lost records and music in a move. They remark that club and fraternity activity has declined, perhaps absorbed by churches.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: And I had all those records down, you know, and I lost them. I used to live around the corner, you know, 4607 Prairie. And I moved from there here. I've been here 27 years. And I lost quite a bit of it. A lot of music, you know, and a lot of records and things like that.
In the moving, isn't it? Yes, in the moving.
They got misplaced, you know, I mean, repertory, you know, and write-ups and things like that. Oh, that's too bad.

I just got a few. I had a large book of them and now I just got a small, I had two, a large one and a small one, so now I have one. They rented out to clubs now, Club De Lisa. I think a couple of colored fellows leased it and then they, and then they rented out to club, for club dates.

Well, there's even less of that to the club activity than there was about 5, 10 years ago. There used to be a lot of clubs, enough to keep Grand Terrace going and De Lisa and so forth. That's right. Now there's even less of the fraternity and club activity. That's true. I suppose that a great deal of it had gone into churches. stuff
